translations.answer: In the HOVER report's 19-DoF Unitree H1, re-directed AMASS, and same-training stack, key-points, joint-angles, and root commands are encoded into a unified space with pattern/masked sparse representations, and then distilled via DAgger from full-body motion teachers. A single policy can cover multiple interfaces, and the results are better than separately trained specialized policies and same-mask multi-mode RL in the same stack. These results do not constitute guarantees for cross-robot or safety-critical switch guarantees.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: All control modes can be represented by subsets of key-body position, local joint-angle, and root commands.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: A full-motion oracle and retargeted AMASS training data are available.
translations.applicability.assumptions.2: Deployment supplies the reported proprioceptive and action history.
translations.applicability.environments.1: reported 20-motion standing evaluation and qualitative locomotion switching
translations.applicability.robots.0: 19-DoF Unitree H1 in the reported setup
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper includes controlled specialist and same-mask multi-mode RL comparisons across five seeds plus a small real-robot evaluation, and official code exposes the corresponding mechanisms. Confidence is capped by the single robot/training family, 20 standing-motion real set, and mostly qualitative runtime switching tests.
